utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness K, good morning. I noticed from the transcript yesterday that omitted to introduce myself. My name is Sayers, and I represent Dario Kordic. When we broke yesterday, we were discussing about the roadblock that was set up outside your village on October 19th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness K, it's true, is it not, that at that time, Bosnian Serb forces were actually launching an assault on the town of Jajce to the west of Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you were aware that there was heavy fighting involved in that assault; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: This is what I heard from some -- secondhand, that is, but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that shortly after the roadblock incident, the town actually fell to the assaulting Bosnian Serb forces, it was captured by them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: It was for reasons that were never explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Following the roadblock incident, you were actually congratulated by commander Refik Lendo over the radio for stopping the HVO troops en route, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: He didn't to me. There was no reason for that and I was not a military person. So I am not aware of any congratulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just read you a statement from your witness statement of February the 15th, 1995 on page 2. "The military BiH commander in Novi Travnik named Lendo congratulated us over the radio or TV for stopping the HVO." Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Such source probably circulated, but you asked me whether I knew of that, and that BH army commander was fighting with the HVO and the Croatian army in the Novi Travnik area. In other words, it had nothing to do with fighting in Jajce because in Jajce, the Catholics, that is, the Croatian army pulled back before the Serb occupiers. That is the real truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. But you do acknowledge making statement that I just read out to the Prosecution's investigators about four and a half years ago; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I don't recall it, but probably I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, you referred during your examination by the Prosecution to a man by the name of Fuad Berbic. It's true, isn't it, that he was the commander of the forces in Ahmici before the road blockade that we've talked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was at the level of the Territorial Defence for an entire region, which included our village as well, in other words, Dubravica, Sivrino Selo, the railroad station, Ahmici, Nadioci, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Mr. Berbic was subsequently replaced immediately before the roadblock incident by Muris Ahmic as the commander of TO forces in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I personally do not know what changes took place there, but it is true that in our village, Muris Ahmic was our sort of immediate commander and Fuad Berbic was transferred and became the officer for the Territorial Defence in the village, the civilian protection in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, let me turn to a related subject, the fighting that occurred on October the 20th of 1992. You have described the casualties on the part of the people that were defending the roadblock. Do you know how many casualties were inflicted upon the Croats, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I really don't know because I was not directly involved. I did not take part in it. When the fighting started, I moved to another part of the village, and so I did not know the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You have described houses catching fire as a result of being hit by tracer fire. Did you actually see that yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I saw smoke, I saw fire, and when we returned to the village, I saw what had happened. But when it was happening, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn to another subject, the subject of -- the unfortunate subject of your cousin who died as a result of being shot at the roadblock on October the 20th. Isn't it true that he was sitting right next to Mr. Sahabudin Muratovic, who was arming an M-84 heavy calibre machine gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was sitting or standing. Sahabudin married a cousin of mine, a relative, and after this event, he said that Halid was killed in his immediate vicinity, and this is why I know the circumstances of his killing. He was the actual witness. He said that he came across the line as a civilian and was killed in his immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Muratovic, though, was actually manning an M-84 heavy calibre machine gun, wasn't he, at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I didn't see what he had, but he probably did have two weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just read you an excerpt from your February the 15th, 1995 statement, and I'd just like you to confirm that this is accurate. "Muratovic, Sabahudin, nicknamed Budo, who had been manning the M-84 machine gun told me that," and I'll omit the name, your cousin, "was next to him when he was shot by a sniper from the area of Ivo Papic's house." Is that statement factually accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I have just confirmed that I received this information from him, and probably at that time he had told me what type of weapon he had, and so I added that to this statement. But I also want to say that all the weapons that we had in the village were -- had come from Slimena, and how shall I put it in military terms, they were practically useless, and had been brought there just for intimidation purposes. There was no real use of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Part of the fighting on October the 20th -- well, actually as the fighting was going on, I believe, you testified, representatives of the HVO actually offered the people manning the blockade the opportunity to avoid further conflict by laying down their arms; that's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say it happened at the barricade, but that during the fighting, the command of the Croatian side and Fuad Berbic held a meeting away from the barricade, perhaps even in the school building. I don't know the location really. But Fuad came to the upper part of the village where we were assembled and said that it had been ordered -- that we had been ordered -- that our people had been ordered to surrender weapons and that the Croatian side would guarantee our safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So the regional commander, Mr. Fuad Berbic, issued these instructions to the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: At that -- yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And as I understand the chronology of events that you related, some people from the region of Zume accepted that offer, laid down their arms, but the soldiers in Ahmici did not want to surrender, and that's when the renewed fighting erupted involving the tracer fire and the other hostilities that you have described; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: It is correct that a part of our -- I cannot say that they were soldiers; they were just armed villagers. In different ways, they had acquired their weapons for the defence of their homes, and since this has become known, that they were armed, then in the -- those in the area of Zume did surrender weapons, but in my village, as you said -- these were not soldiers. These were common people who had faulty weapons from Slimena and some hunting rifles and their personal pistols, and those were the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K, if you can deal briefly with these questions, we'll get through your evidence. Mr. Sayers, there's no need to go over a matter which we've been over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I agree entirely, Your Honour, and I will try to avoid doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It is true, Witness K, that after the event that you've just described when the forces in Ahmici refused to lay down their arms, that Mr. Muris Ahmic was continuously calling the army headquarters to request assistance; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I don't know because I really was not involved in these military matters. I was just a common citizen who was trying to save his family and his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Did you state to the Prosecution's investigators in 1995, "During the attack, Muris Ahmic continuously called BiH headquarters in Vitez for help but no one was sent to help"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I believe that I did say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't mean to imply anything by these questions, sir. It was a long time ago and memories fade, but let me just ask you this: After the fighting ended, you gave some testimony about the military police from the HVO patrolling your village to ensure that no houses were looted. You actually had left your house unlocked during the hostilities; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I did not have the time to close it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. But when you returned to your village, nothing had been taken from your house. That's the point I'm trying to make; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to another subject, you had mentioned a conversation or a statement supposedly made by a Mr. Valenta on TV in Split to the effect that Croats in Vitez must prepare themselves for a struggle against Muslims. Didn't he later contend that that was a slip of the tongue and that what he meant was that the Croats generally had to prepare themselves for a struggle against Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, he said that first version publicly on television, and I heard, I wasn't present, that he then denied that in a smaller circle, that he said that he misspoke. But what he said originally went out into the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn to another subject, which was the hostilities that broke out in your village on April the 16th and the events that immediately preceded them. Did you know that -- or did you ever hear that a number of HVO soldiers had been captured outside of Novi Travnik by Mujahedin on April the 13th, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Anything is possible, but I really didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about the kidnapping of commander Zivko Totic in Zenica on the night of April the 14th/15th, and the murder of his four bodyguards and one civilian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I heard that and this was also in the media, in the mass media, television and so on, but obviously I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Isn't it true that on the night of April the 15th, you were actually on patrol in Ahmici with your brother? And I won't mention his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. We were near our houses. There were no patrols. There was no duty to patrol. We just came out in our backyards because our houses were adjoining, so we were just there, outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying you were not on guard duty that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sorry. Is that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Because we were at our homes. We were on no official patrol. We came out to just look around our houses because our houses are a bit separated out in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let me just read you a statement or an excerpt from a statement that you gave to the Centre for Investigating War Crimes and crimes of genocide against Muslims on May the 4th, 1993. "On 15th April, 1993 from 12 until 24.00, I was on guard duty in the village." Do you remember telling the investigators for that institution, what I have just read, about six years ago, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Perhaps, how shall I put it, it was written down erroneously. I know that the hours do not make sense, 12 to 24. We perhaps went out around 10.00 in the evening, and it was no patrol. It was just myself and my brother. The family stayed indoors, and it was a regular thing, a usual thing, for us to come out and see that everything was all right around because there were tensions at that time. And the statements given 20 days after those horrors over there, it is possible that the investigators or even the typist had added something, that I was part of a patrol, because I didn't even have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sayers, we've got to move forward. You can ask the witness whether there was a village association with a type of rotating guard whose duty it was to watch over the village and to help guard the villagers. I'd like that question to be asked of the witness so that we can understand this. But we've got to get forward on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I agree entirely, Your Honour, and we will try to do precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness K, you heard His Honour's question. Would you please provide the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, there was, but it was all part of the civilian protection. These were not military structures. There was a manned -- that is, there were people who assigned villagers to be on duty. There were not any armed guards. They were not ready to engage in any fighting. If any kind of shelling or attack occurred, they would be in charge of rousing the villagers so that we could evacuate our homes. And there was also a list of these people so that there wouldn't always be the same people. So some people were in charge of these assignments, so that certain people would not always be on duty and certain people, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. It was during this period of time that you -- this is the night of April the 15th -- that you actually noticed troop movements in the vicinity of the Kupreskic houses involving people in full combat gear; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No, those was not troops. Those were two men who I saw -- they were my neighbours who were HVO members. There were no troops, just two soldiers whom I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well. Isn't it true that you actually informed your army command of this immediately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: You constantly associate me with the military. I just reported to this civilian officer that there was something going on. That was my duty. So I told him so that he would then, through the channels, get information whether there was an impending attack or something else coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just read you one statement from the interview that you gave to the investigating judge, Dijana Ajanovic on December the 15th, 1993 on page 2. You described seeing people "going in full combat gear towards the Kupreskic houses. We immediately informed our army command of this and were told that we should not arouse panic, that it did not mean anything as far as an attack was concerned." Do you remember telling the investigating judge that, Mr. K?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I told her that I had noticed people, soldiers, that I informed the representatives of the civilian protection, that is, the man in charge, and that he told me not to start any panic, that there will be no attack. So what she did is she just summarised this into one single sentence and perhaps created some confusion. He told us not to panic, that nothing would happen, that there was no danger of an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But isn't it true, sir, that you actually went to bed fully dressed because you were expecting something to happen? You kept thinking that something was about to happen, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: My son was already in the camp in Busovaca at that time, and I walked around my house, as I have already said, after midnight, so, indeed, I just took off my jacket and shoes and lay down in trousers. I couldn't sleep ever since my son had been imprisoned, so I just lay down to take a rest, not really going to bed properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. When the assault on your village started, isn't it true that calls were made to the 3rd Corps for help through a radio transmitter located in the house of Nasid Ahmic; that is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to see that, and later on, the women were saying that one of the women had called up by phone, she had a relative down there, and informed him that such and such a thing was happening. He allegedly told her, because that is what I heard from this woman, that we should just lie down on the floor in our houses, that we should not panic, that negotiations were ongoing, and that things would stop. That was the answer she got, apparently, from Zenica. We didn't have any radio links with Zenica because that is quite some way away. We only had radio links with people in Vitez, with those bodies in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's all of the questions I have on that subject, sir. One question: After you went to Zenica in May 1993 and thereafter, were you ever employed by the Institute for the Investigation of Crimes Against Humanity in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. I was a member of the civil defence and I was mostly working in the field, in the area controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I carried food to people on the front lines and that sort of thing. I may have also spoken to people as I went along, but I didn't have any official capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, and I don't propose to spend more than 30 seconds on this, I would just like the usher to show Witness K the statement he made to the investigating judge on December the 15th, 1993 and which is signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness K, I'd just like you to turn to the last page and verify that that is, indeed, your signature. Did you say "yes," sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is my signature. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you just read into the record what your occupation was listed as, sir, on page 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: That is not my occupation. I was a member of the civil defence, and on behalf of our municipality, I had the work obligation to occasionally join, with respect to the local people of Ahmici, and take a few statements from them, and maybe that was the reason why this was written down. By occupation, I'm an engineer of work organisations, so this was not my occupation, nor was it my preoccupation during the war. The only truth is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. What is the occupation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Engineer industrial relations employed at the Institute for Investigation of Crimes against Humanity, Zenica, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. No. No. No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, have you elicited what this institute does?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I have not, and that seems a good point at which to pose the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Witness K, could you please let the Trial Chamber know what the Institute for the Investigation of Crimes against Humanity in Zenica actually did or does?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: The aim of the institute, as far as I am aware, is to collect information and other evidence which would help the Tribunal in the discovery of war criminals. I said that I did take several statements from my neighbours, but I was never officially employed by that institute, and who put these words after the comma, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The final topic that I'd like to discuss with you is the statements that you described as having been made by Mr. Kordic supposedly on Busovaca TV. Do I understand, sir, that these comments were made, according to you anyway, during the course of a press conference at which there were multiple participants? The ones I'm talking about now are the ones in November 1992 that you described.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes. There were journalists and there were three participants, Kordic, Kostroman, and Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How long did this press conference actually last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I don't know how long it lasted because I didn't watch it from the beginning, and especially when I heard the comments, I had had enough, so I didn't even wait for it to end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You didn't actually attach very much significance to the comments that you've described as having been made by Mr. Kordic, nor did your friends and acquaintances, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: The contrary. I took it very seriously, and not just me but everyone else who saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, sir. Isn't it true that after meetings between the Croat representatives and Muslim representatives of the parties involved in the conflict at the barricade, an agreement was reached, and that agreement was actually jointly broadcast immediately afterwards on TV RBIH and on HVO Television.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Probably there was some sort of an agreement, but after the conflict, because by joint forces of Croatian and Muslim officials, an agreement was reached, and all the damage that was done was repaired jointly. However, as I know, before the conflict -- no, I'm sorry. No, I'm sorry. That was before the 16th of April, not the 20th of October. I'm sorry. From that moment on, we lived together and relations were relatively good until the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you to verify that this is what you told the investigating judge six years ago: That you had held several meetings, that there were meetings between the Croat and Muslim representatives of the battling forces, "We adopted conclusions on mutual non-aggression and mutual assistance. These conclusions were read on TV RBIH and HVO television which was broadcast from Vitez and that gave us a certain sense of security," and then you describe the statements supposedly made by Mr. Kordic and went on to say that "but we did not attach much significance to that statement, especially because we got together later and thought there wouldn't be any more problems." That's what you actually told the investigating --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: That is correct, but these meetings that we had frequently were held by ordinary people, ordinary citizens, without any political or military persons being present. It was just agreements amongst ourselves, and it is true that at one meeting where I kept the record and a Croat, I think his name was Josipovic, he was a forester and he was appreciated in our village, we made this record, together with conclusions. And I personally was asked to carry those conclusions to Vitez Television, which was held then by the Croatian people. Also in Stari Vitez, we had our own local television, and I also took a copy of that record containing an agreement on non-aggression, and both radio stations broadcast this. But all this was at the local level, not the television of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, sir. So you actually facilitated the television broadcasts or participated in the process by which information was disseminated over the television yourself, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. I just gave them a letter or, rather, a piece of paper which they read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just a couple of questions on the subject of the various competing propaganda organs. You actually did not like to watch or listen to radio or TV carrying Croat propaganda, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Would you? Of course I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that the Muslim residents of your area responded to the Croat propaganda by broadcasting propaganda of their own, both on TV and radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Probably, but to a much lesser extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And one final question. Isn't it true that you actually didn't own a TV in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: You're saying that I didn't have a TV set? Of course I had a TV set.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Not one, but two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. At page 2927 of your testimony in the Kupreskic case, let me just read you what you said. You were asked whether you'd seen the TV programme, and you said, "I didn't watch that programme because, first of all, I do not own a TV set." Do you remember testifying to that effect on September the 24th of last year, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: For me, that case is over and I wouldn't like to go back to it, but I think I didn't say that because that would be lying myself -- I would be lying to myself, and that can be verified. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Page 2927, lines 23 through 25 of the transcript in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, is it disputed that Mr. Kordic said on the television programme "that Ahmici would pay a dear price for putting up the barricade, it would be razed to the ground"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It is disputed, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K, you hear that, that it's disputed. Did Mr. Kordic say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The other matter which I should have also raised really with Mr. Mikulicic is the accuracy of the lists of victims which this witness has prepared, together with the maps. Is there any challenge to the accuracy of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence cannot, at this point in time, affirm whether each individual name on that list is correct, but as a matter of principle, the Defence is not challenging the fact that in Ahmici there were many victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: A point that was just examined a few minutes ago about whether there was a television set that the witness spoke about during his testimony in the Kupreskic case, that was 2927. The question was asked by one of the Defence counsel in that case, Mr. Radovic, the question was the following -- the witness was asked: "When you arrived in Zenica, did you perhaps see a television programme in which Sakib Ahmic was in the hospital?" And the answer was, "I didn't see that -- I wasn't able to see the programme because I didn't have a television." However, at the time of the facts that we're speaking about, Witness K, the programme of Sakib Ahmic on television was broadcast, whereas you were already in Zenica and that the attack on the village of Ahmici had taken place. So this is after the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just objection to the form of that question, Your Honour, because the actual statement on the lines that I read is: "I didn't see that. I didn't watch that programme, because, first of all, I do not own a TV set, but I did hear that there was a programme of that kind."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the issue, without going into it in any detail, is whether the witness owned a television set when he was in Ahmici prior to the 15th of April. Now, that is the point. Witness K, did you own a television at that stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I had two TV sets. I had a car; I had everything. When I reached Zenica, I had nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So the position in Zenica at the time of that broadcast was that you didn't own a set; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may ask the question so that there will be no questions about the testimony in the Kupreskic case, that we could put the testimony into this in its entirety, so you can see what the context was when that was given in September of 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that's necessary, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if you would like to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In general, about this subject in respect of the Defence and for the Prosecution, when there is a degree of flexibility when referring to the transcripts and to reports of other trials, one has to be careful that quotations are taken -- be careful that the quotations are not taken out of their context, because the Chamber always have the ability to verify this. But it's a waste of time to quote things outside their context, which certainly does not make our work any easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to have a correction made here. It was said a few minutes ago or written in the transcript, on page 6822, 6-8-2-2, line 8, when a reference was made to a record of the witness before the investigating judge, it was said that the television programme was broadcast from Vitez had created a feeling of insecurity. In the transcript, it speaks about a feeling of security, safety, not lack of security. I would like to have the transcript corrected, the transcript for that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness K, a few minutes ago in respect of weaponry, which some of the inhabitants of Ahmici had, you said that they were weapons that came from the Slimena weapons depot. Those weapons from Slimena, weren't most of them weapons which had been picked up by some of the Muslims after they had been left there, partly destroyed, when that depot was attacked by the HVO in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. Younger, braver people went there because there were mine fields, and they went to collect what was left, the weapons that had been burnt, that really couldn't be used, but people collected them to repair them and to use them as weapons for defence. That was our only source of armaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness K, on several occasions, allusions were made to prior statements that you made before the Zenica investigating judge or the institute for research into crimes against humanity in Zenica. In those statements, it is indicated regularly that when you say "We did this or we did that or we were congratulated, we sent a message," when that phraseology is used, isn't that simply a way of speaking to refer to the Muslims in general and not to you in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, absolutely so. When I say "they," I'm referring to the other party, the Croats, the Catholics, and the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness K, you were asked a question a few minutes ago about the congratulations that were given to you. When I say you, you understand now that that means the Muslims, were congratulated for having stopped the HVO troops that were going through Ahmici on the 19th of October, 1992. And you said that those congratulations came from Mr. Refik Lendo who was the chief of the Novi Travnik brigade for the BH army. Why, in your opinion, did the chief of the Novi Travnik brigade congratulate you for having stopped the troops that were going through Jajce and not in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I really never saw or heard those congratulations, but I heard them being repeated around. As for your question, perhaps you should ask the Defence because really, how did they know where that army was going, where those troops were going? We didn't even know that those troops were coming. This was spontaneous so we really had no plans, or at least our people who put up the barricade, their aim was because they were disarmed, they wanted to collect arms again. That was their purpose. That was their aim.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'm merely asking you, Witness K, that according to the information that you had at that time, the HVO that was never stopped in Ahmici that day were, in fact, going to Novi Travnik; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes. That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. Two more questions about the events of the 16th of April. Do you remember that on the 16th of April, 1993, that that was a Friday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Does Friday have a special meaning for Muslims? Is that a special day for the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Certainly. It is the day when the Muslims of a dzemat, an entire area, perform prayers together in mosques jointly, collectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You said that after having gone with those few who had escaped from the village of Zenica that you had been asked by many institutions who questioned you about what had happened in Ahmici, specifically the Institute for Criminal Research?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Each one of us received a host of questions from all kinds of people, journalists and all sorts of other people, but we wanted to tell them what had happened. We wanted the world to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Throughout that period that you spent in Zenica, starting in April 1993 and continuing until today, this is now 1999, was there any type of organisation or Bosnian Croat investigators who ever questioned you about what happened in Ahmici on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I was not approached by such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: May I just correct myself? I am now living in my own village. Thanks to God, I returned in May, so I'm no longer in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K, thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give your evidence. You are now released. Let me make use of this opportunity of a break in the proceedings to announce the change of hours next week due to our hospital appointments. On Tuesday, that's Tuesday the 21st, we shall not be able to start until 11.30. Yes, the witness can go out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And we will sit until about 5.00 that day. On Friday the 24th, we shall not start until 10.00. Apart from that, of course, the hours will be the same. Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you allow me, I would like to point out to the Chamber that because of certain difficulties that we had with the witness who arrived late, we worked with the witness very late last night, and the last part of the discussion that we ordinarily have with the witnesses is being completed. The Office of the Prosecutor would be very grateful to the Trial Chamber if it would agree to the break a little earlier so that we can -- until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And you would be ready to call the witness then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will take the break now and start again at five past eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, we will sit now and then go on slightly past the hour and a half to quarter to one, and we will sit again at 2.15 and go on until 4.00. I hope that will be acceptable to all, including those in the booths. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. Yesterday, I had taken an undertaking that everything would be prepared so that the witness would be able to testify today. This undertaking was honoured, it had some difficulties for me and for our office, but we were able to hear the testimony of this witness. I would simply say that the witness who arrived last night late asked for certain protective measures, and I ask you, if possible, for this to be a private session so that we can present to you the arguments in support of that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, starting at the point where you had the functions, began to work in the municipality between 1990 and the spring of 1992, is it true that the municipal government in Vitez was functioning properly; that is, that there were no difficulties between the Muslims and Croats in respect of the administration of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During that period in September of 1991, was there a joint crisis council established in the municipality because of the war that was raging in Croatia against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, it was set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you yourself have responsibilities within that crisis council?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During that period of time, Croats from Vitez, as well as the Bosniaks from the municipality of Vitez, did they go to Croatia to fight on the side of the Croats against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did the crisis council decide at that time that explosives and gunpowder could be sold to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In 1991, Witness L, the individual whose name is Anto Valenta, who was the president of the HDZ in Vitez, wrote a book called "The Partition of Bosnia and its Struggle for Integrity," a book which talked about the various options of the partition of Bosnia-Hercezgovina and in which it was suggested that that would be a way of resolving ethnic problems there. Are you aware of that book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Before the book was published during 1991, its author, Anto Valenta, asked you to read his manuscript and to make some comments, some criticisms, on the document but that you refused to do that at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Therefore, you had a copy of the manuscript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And then the book itself once it was published; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I am going to show you a copy of the book and ask you to tell us whether, in fact, this is the book that we're speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say that there is a version in Bosnian Croat and one in English. The document in Bosnian Croat is Z9, as is the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, are you going to refer to this book at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply am going to ask the witness whether this document, which was already referred to during other testimony, is, in fact, the book that was shown to the witness at that time and which is published by Mr. Anto Valenta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, could you tell us whether, during the conversations that you had with Mr. Valenta, whom you knew, what was the essence of those conversations? What were Mr. Valenta's comments about the possible partition according to the ethnic groups of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: He analysed the ethnic composition, and in a sense, he advocated the resettlement of populations from one territory to another, so that three different areas with ethnically pure populations would be formed, the Serbs, Croats, and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Since you said that you saw the manuscript and the final version of the book, did you notice whether there were any differences between the manuscript that had been given to you and the final version?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: There were some differences. There were several versions of the delineation; there were different dividing lines. There was one, as far as I can remember, going from Mostar to Stolac and the option with the dividing line going through Neum had not existed in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. We're going to move forward in time a little bit, Witness L, and we get to the end of April 1992 at the time that the HVO and the Territorial Defence agreed to organise a joint attack on the depot, which at that time still belonged to the federal army, that is, the JNA, and that the depot was in Stolac and that it was called Slimena. According to the agreement, once the weapons were seized, they would be distributed equally between the HVO and the BH army, and, in fact, that is not what happened and that the HVO alone attacked the depot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And that the HVO forces went to Slimena two days before the agreed date, the date that had been agreed on jointly for the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: That is how I was informed by the TO commander, though I wasn't participating in these things, but I think that is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: According to the information which you received at that time, the attack was carried out under the command of Colonel Filipovic, but also by the accused, Mario Cerkez. This is the information you received; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I think something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You received information also from the commander of the Territorial Defence, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And you had regular meetings with that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, we did have contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: We're speaking about Sefkija Dzidic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. At that time, it was Hakija Cengic who was the commander of the TO when these things were being decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move forward in 1992. At the beginning of 1992, there was a radio station, a joint radio station composed of Bosniaks and Croats in Vitez that was found in the municipal building. Is it true that in May of 1992, Anto Valenta, about whom we've already spoken, came to the municipal building, took away the radio equipment and the radio facilities of the town, and that an exclusively Croat-controlled radio was set up in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it also true that at the time, the HVO in Vitez, the HVO set up a television station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the evening of 19 June, 1992, Witness L, the municipal building and the police station were taken over by a group of HOS soldiers, as they were known at that time, and they were under the command of Darko Kraljevic. On that same day, you had a meeting where Ivica Santic was not, which you chaired and in which Anto Valenta was a participant.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: That was the next day. (redacted) (redacted), I chaired the meeting, and it was held the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it true that during that meeting, Mr. Anto Valenta said to you that it was the HOS that was responsible for the takeover of the police station and the municipal building, and also added that the HVO should be able to control everything and protect everybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In general, didn't the HVO, whenever acts were committed against the Muslims, dreadful acts, wouldn't they ordinarily or regularly blame the extremists or members of HOS as being the perpetrators of those acts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And the HVO would also say during those meetings that they had no control over the members of the HOS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Around the 20th of June, 1992, Witness L, that you were invited to participate in a television broadcast at Vitez TV about the events that had taken place the day before with that same Anto Valenta, but that you refused in the end, refused to participate in the broadcast because you didn't want your statements to be prerecorded and you wanted to be able to make live statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Let me just clarify this. I was in the TV studio and we wanted to address the citizens of Vitez, to calm them down. However, there was some delay, they wanted to tape this programme, and eventually I did not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Isn't it true that one of the journalists who had invited you had prepared a list of questions for you and also a list of answers to those same questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Actually, it wasn't a list. He tried to guide me in that sense by posing certain questions and saying that he more or less knew what answers I would give.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And that's what eventually persuaded you not to participate in the broadcast; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1992, Witness L, did the executive board of the SDA party, which considered that the establishment of the authorities of Herceg-Bosna and the HVO in Vitez was illegal, decide to form a coordination board for the protection of the interests of the Muslims in the municipality, and that you yourself were appointed as president of that committee; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: A document was published the next day in order to announce the establishment of that coordination board for protection. I'm going to show you the document, which is an exhibit, Z162-1. I ask that you read this, which is dated the 12th of July, 1992, and specifically, the next-to-last paragraph where the issue of the Muslims of Vitez is discussed. Could you read this document for us, please, the next-to-last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: "The Muslims of Vitez do not recognise the HVO of Herceg-Bosna as an organ of authority and they will consider their decisions invalid. The Muslims of Vitez will respect the legally elected authorities, future changes only if they are in conformity with valid laws, the decisions of the Vitez municipal assembly and the platform of the BH state presidency."

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you agree with that statement completely, Witness L?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The legal authorities at that time that you were thinking about were those that were the result of the elections of 1990, which brought you and Mr. Santic to the municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In respect of that coordinating board, did it function for several months and, during that time, publish various announcements? I will show you a second document, which is dated the 10th of September, 1992, which is Exhibit number Z210-1, Z210-1. Thank you for reading this document as well. Do you recognise it as one of the documents published by the coordination board, whose chairman you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it true that in September 1992, the 10th of September, 1992, buildings that belonged to your party in Vitez were the subject of explosions? In fact, they were destroyed by explosions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, there was an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you file a complaint at that time about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I think that the MUP was informed and that it carried out an on-site inspection. The police station was informed and carried out an on-site inspection, the police station in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: As far as you know, did the investigation end up identifying those responsible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Somewhat later in 1992, Witness L, on the 19th of October, 1992 exactly, while a conflict had just started in Novi Travnik, there were HVO forces who were supposed to go through the Vitez municipality in order to reinforce the HVO forces in Novi Travnik. During that evening of the 19th of October, 1992, did you yourself attend a meeting at the headquarters of the BH army at the Vitez high school where Ivica Santic and the accused, Mario Cerkez, arrived around 8.00 in the evening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, I think from now on you should stop leading and let the witness give the evidence, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the meeting of the 19th of October, 1992, Witness L, what were the requests that were made by Mr. Cerkez and Mr. Santic, made to the commander of the territorial forces, that is, the defence forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: They asked that the barricades in Vitez be removed. In fact, those were the barricades in Ahmici and Grbavica, in two areas of Vitez where the Territorial Defence had erected them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Grbavica is sometimes also called Divjak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: You could say so, even though those of us who live in Vitez distinguish between the two. One is part of another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Out of a desire to calm the conflict down that was going on in Novi Travnik and which could extend to Travnik, did you suggest to Mr. Santic that you might use your services in order to intervene and to act by going to Novi Travnik yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: No. I proposed that we go to Novi Travnik in order to try to calm down the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What was Mr. Santic's answer when you made the suggestion that you could go to Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: He said that he had spoken there and that nothing would happen but that I could try myself, and he gave me a phone number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you say that he told you that he had spoken with them, at least in the French version that's what I heard, whom are you speaking about? Whom are you thinking about, and to whom did Mr. Santic speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Since he had given me Kordic's number, I assume that he had spoken to Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Santic had said to you that he already had spoken to Mr. Kordic, and what was Mr. Kordic's reaction during that initial conversation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just object to the form of that question, Your Honour. I believe the witness said that he assumed that Mr. Santic had spoken to Mr. Kordic because he had been given Mr. Kordic's number. The question assumes that there was a conversation between Mr. Santic and Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness L, can you tell us what Mr. Santic said about that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Just that he had spoken to him and that there would be nothing of it, that I could try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: When you say "him," to whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Probably, since he gave me a number in Travnik and said that it was Kordic, I assumed that he probably had spoken to Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This telephone number -- you said the telephone number was in Travnik. It was really in Novi Travnik; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Novi Travnik, yes. Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you yourself telephoned that number in Novi Travnik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is something on the transcript where the witness answered, "Just that he had spoken to him and that there would be nothing of it, that I could try." I want to find out what is meant by "there would be nothing of it." That's how it is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, could you tell us exactly, even if that goes back several years, could you tell us exactly what Mr. Santic said that you then related further to that conversation with the accused, Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Just as I stated there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think in English, the effect of the evidence must be that the witness is saying that Santic said nothing would come of it or that nothing had come of it, because in the English version "nothing of it" is meaningless.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, when Mr. Santic said to you that nothing had come of that previous conversation, what was he, in fact, speaking about, he and the accused, Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just one objection to the form of that question too, if I may. I think that it would be unobjectionable if the witness were asked, "What did Mr. Santic actually say?" But it's highly objectionable for the witness to speculate as to what may have been in Mr. Santic's mind but not expressed when he made the comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, once again, could you try to search your memory and to remember what it is that Mr. Santic said to you after that time, after he had called the accused, Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I hate to bounce up, Your Honour, but once again the form of that question assumes precisely the issue that trying to establish here, and I think it's objectionable as phrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I disagree. Let the question be put again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, could you once again rely on your memory and try to tell us what, at the time, Mr. Santic said to you after he had called the accused, Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: That the conversation had taken place and that the results of the conversation amounted to nothing, that there was no solution. I'm just trying to clarify the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did Mr. Santic say to you at that time that Dario Kordic did not want to listen to what he was saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, you mustn't ask that. Let's move on from here. Let's go on to the next passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you yourself called that number that Mr. Santic had given you in Novi Travnik, did you not speak directly then with Dario Kordic, or with somebody else? Do you remember what that other person said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: To wait, that I would get through because he was busy, he was negotiating.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So you held the telephone for a few minutes and you heard what was on the other end of the line. Did you hear the accused, Dario Kordic, speaking in the room where he was at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it was that Dario Kordic was saying at that point, the words that you heard over the telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: It had to do with Vitez and what was going on there and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you have the feeling from what you had heard that Mr. Kordic was excited?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Let the witness describe how he found Mr. Kordic. What impression did you form?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: It is possible that the voice was a bit excited. That is my impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you hear Mr. Kordic say anything or swearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: There was something of that too, but the gist, as I said, was what I just stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Witness L, you explained to the accused at that time that you and Santic were considering going to Novi Travnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Dario Kordic's answer was when you made that suggestion to go to Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: In fact, the goal was to try to calm down the situation so that things would return to normal, and the response was, there were several conditions. Yes, if I would be able to do this, if the army would lay down their weapons, I said that I was not competent for that and that Santic and I would come as citizens of Vitez and as neighbours, and the conversation ended there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the conversation, did you speak about the commander of the Novi Travnik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that was a condition. That was said, that the brigade commander surrenders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So Dario Kordic said two conditions: the laying down of the arms by the Muslims and then that their chief would surrender, Refik Lendo; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Kordic because you had spoken to him previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: We did know each other. We had had contacts on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Had you met him on several occasions at various meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, in passing, at meetings, and things like that. We knew each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that it might be -- that there might have been a different person at the end of the line, different from Dario Kordic, on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I think it was Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You think that or you're sure it was Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: If I think, then I'm certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Also in October 1992, Witness L, Ivica Santic, as the president of the municipality, issued a new type of employment contracts for those people who were working there and said that those who did not sign this new type of contract would lose their job; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it true that about ten employees of the municipality at that time refused to sign the contract and, therefore, lost their positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it true that among them there was an architect, a construction businessman, and then a chief of services for the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During November 1992, did you receive a document with an HVO heading and which informed you that you had become the vice-president of the HVO in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: The HVO government, not the HVO. The HVO government.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The document which came from the HVO government, since you're speaking about the Vitez government, I think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And in the end, you refused to sign the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you explain why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: For the reason which was defined by that announcement. It was not in accordance with the law and all the other regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When we get to 1993, that is, April 1993, on the 15th of April, 1993, Mr. L, you were part of a meeting with the chiefs of the BH army in Vitez, specifically Mr. Dzidic, Mr. Sivro, and the police representative, Mr. Mahmutovic, who themselves said that they were coming back from a meeting with the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I was present. That was a meeting of the presidency, and I was told -- they said that to everyone who was present there. There were another seven or eight people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: After the meeting that these people we've just mentioned had with the HVO, did Mr. Dzidic, Mr. Mahmutovic, and Mr. Sivro, were they -- did they show any kind of concerns, fear that there was an imminent danger of a conflict breaking out with the HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: They said, and, in fact, you could feel that the situation was tense, but they said that there would be no conflict with the HVO and that another joint meeting would be held the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During that same evening of the 15th of April, 1993, sometime in the evening, is it true that you received at home, in your apartment in Kolonija, an anonymous phone call from somebody who was saying that he was going to come to your house and get you and arrest you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive such a call.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it true that on the next day, 16 April, around 5.15 in the morning, there was another phone call in your house in Kolonija and that during the phone call, your wife answered and recognised Mrs. Ankica Jukic's voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Mrs. Ankica Jukic, who was one of the wives of the members of the HVO said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: She said, "Where are you going to go now, balijas?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: "Where are you going now?" After the phone call, did you notice in the neighbourhood where you lived that there were soldiers wearing helmets or masks over their heads; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And so with your family, you decided to go to seek shelter in the apartment of a friend, a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you learn, after you had left your apartment, that HVO soldiers had come and had shot into the door of your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I was told this by Dzevad, my neighbour, a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you also notice that the doors of the building which you lived in, which ordinarily were closed at night, locked at night, had all been unlocked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the 15th of April, from the apartment where you were taking shelter, that there were soldiers who had taken up positions in the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: You can't say that they had taken up positions. Some people were in front of the building, and among them were some of my neighbours. So you cannot say that they had taken up positions. That means something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Among the soldiers who were there in front of your building, did you recognise a person named Marijan Vinac, who came from the village of Donja Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, he was also there. We lived in the same building; he was a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And that Marijan Vinac also lived in Kolonija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The soldiers that you're speaking to us about, were they wearing black uniforms or were they wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: For the most part, they were, I believe, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At some point, did you hear that same individual, Marijan Vinac, saying your name and also saying that you should be somewhere and that you wouldn't be able to escape; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: In fact, he said that I was around here and that I couldn't flee anywhere, that I was around. That is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you feel at that time that soldiers, along with Marijan Vinac, were looking for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I could infer from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And so you remained in the apartment of the individual who was sheltering you for about four days, and then on the 18th of April, 1993, about 30 minutes before there was a large explosion that took place, you heard that same Marijan Vinac giving instructions to the people in the building to open up their windows; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: After the explosion, did you hear that same Marijan Vinac expressing reassuring words to the Croatian people in the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The next day, 19 April, 1993, were you finally taken prisoner and taken to the basement of the cinema building where you found other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: There were about 200 detainees, all men, aged from about 17 to 60 years old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the evening of 19 April, you saw Dr. Mujezinovic, who was going into the basement and who was escorted by a soldier, and Dr. Mujezinovic asked you to go with him in order to participate in negotiations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: A meeting took place between you and Dr. Mujezinovic and other Muslim dignitaries from Vitez in an office on the first floor of that cinema building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At that meeting on the Croat side, there were men named Boro Jozic and Zvonko Cilic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: These two people, did they ask you and the other Muslims to contact the military authorities of the BH army in order to put a stop to the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: There were several phone calls made. You were not able to reach General Hadzihasanovic and, therefore, you called his deputy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you able to refuse to make those phone calls, you, Witness L, and the other individuals who were there in that same situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you in a position to refuse to make those phone calls? Did you have a choice or were you forced to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: There were no direct threats, but we were detained so it was expected of us to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What was normal, Witness L, to do what you were asked to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Well, to call, to establish contact, to start talks in order to stop this, and this would be beneficial to those of us who were detained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: While those negotiations were going on, do you remember that the fighting was continuing, raging in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: You could hear shooting. There was fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the end of those initial contacts that you had with Mr. Cilic, Jozic finally asked you to negotiate with other well-known people. Who were those other well-known people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: They had already come there to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'm asking whether you asked to negotiate with other well-known people, other dignitaries, other than Mr. Jozic and Mr. Cilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Well, yes, we requested that if we were going to be negotiating, that we negotiate with some competent people, not with Cilic and Jozic. We didn't consider them as competent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the end, it was Mr. Skopljak or Mr. Santic who came; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you reach an agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: Well, we did. We drafted a written document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The negotiations that we were just speaking about, were they carried out under duress, Witness L?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: The very fact that you are detained is pressure. There were no direct threats, no one was threatening us, but we were in detention and we had no choice. There was no direct threat, but it was under pressure due to the very fact that we were in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a document, Witness L. This is a document dated 20 April, 1993, which refers, among other things, to those negotiations and which has reference number Z751. Could you read the last part of the first paragraph where mention is made of that, the evening of 19 April 1993, et cetera? Could you read that to us out loud, that passage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: "In the evening of the 19th of April, 1993, from the direction of the village of Gacice, the enemy fired most probably with a 82-millimetre recoilless gun, three projectiles, on the command post of the Viteska Brigade. There were no casualties; only material damage."

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'm not sure that the French interpretation matches exactly what's here. I think that things were turned around, that the -- I understood that the firing was coming from Gacice and they were directed onto the brigade post. All right. Referring again to this same document, I'm going to ask you to read the last paragraph where the meeting and negotiations we are speaking about are referred to. Could you read us that passage out loud, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K [Resumes]
utterances.text: "On the premises of the Viteska Brigade command, prominent representatives of Muslims gathered during the night with the goal of finding a way to stop the armed conflict.
